already-have.corrections: Deltas and adjacent prior art the proposal should cite rather than claim as fully absent: (1) Issue #249 (OPEN, "22: supply-chain + provisioning attestation") already plans boot-time STM32 anti-counterfeit probes (CPUID/UID/DHUK-probe/errata fingerprinting) plus triple-UID binding and SE050/OPTIGA attestation — a chip-identity fingerprint, not a bus-impedance one; D-02 is the complementary board-level layer and should be filed as a sibling of #249/#68, not folded into it. (2) #249 notes the #36 consequence: the factory never runs at RDP>=1 so a per-die DHUK fingerprint cannot be factory-enrolled — the same RDP-0 factory stage is fine for D-02 because the RC baseline does not depend on DHUK, but the enrolment write must go to a per-device page outside the FSBL range and outside pages 123-127 (page 126 = DHUK-wrapped BHK, 127 = first-boot journal/salt, 123/124/125 = counters/attempts/admin-wipe) — or to OTP, which needs the #36 OTP-layout owner. (3) The content side of the same threat already has partial mitigation in-tree: F-24 stage E constant-time blitter / seed-wizard decoy rendering (red-teaming.md §7.7 lines 761-765; issues #258 decoy-flicker re-test, #260 constant-pixel-count encoding, #784 restore-wizard letters bypassing the blitter) — these raise the cost of glyph-template matching on a sniffed SPI stream but detect nothing; D-02 is the detection side and should be scoped as such. (4) The #705 lesson is slightly broader than stated: PB15's reset MODER is analog so IDR reads 0 regardless; the proposal correctly requires digital-input/OD configuration, but note the retracted probe was deleted partly because it ran on EVERY boot of every build — D-02's boot-time check needs to be gated so it does not repeat that cost on bench/QEMU builds. (5) Consumption-mask coupling: on pq1 the mask runs on TIM3_CH1/PA6 (NC pad), not PA5; PA5 is SCK. The proposal's "pause the mask" requirement still applies because PA6 is physically adjacent to PA5/PA7 and the mask is production-forced, but the pin identification should read PA6, not "mask-adjacent PA5". (6) Could not check: whether any owner conversation outside the repo/issues (e.g. the 2026-07-21 session transcripts in the worktree root) accepted the display-bus implant as a permanent residual; the mcp codex server was unavailable this session so no external-model cross-check was run.

feasible.reason: The physics is sound and realisable on pq1 without a hardware change: STM32U5 internal pull-up is 25-55 kOhm (typ ~40k), so a 15-30 pF display net gives tau ~0.6-1.2 us = 100-190 cycles at 160 MHz (secure/src/hw/spi_hw.rs:133 confirms 160 MHz; DWT CYCCNT is already used in secure/src/hw/lcd_nv3007.rs and main.rs), and a 3-10 pF implant input is a 15-50% shift. A passive resistor-isolated tap cannot hide its capacitance and still sniff 20 MHz SPI (spi_hw.rs:183-201: SCK = 160/8 = 20 MHz): to be invisible against a 40k pull-up the series R must be >>40k, which with ~5 pF of implant input gives a tau of microseconds, far slower than the 50 ns bit period. So the cheap implant class the threat names is genuinely caught; only a FET/comparator-buffered tap (~1 pF), a non-contact capacitive/EM pickup (<0.5 pF), or a full panel/flex replacement that re-centres the band evades it, and the proposal states that floor. The secure world owns SPI1 and GPIOA (spi_hw.rs:116-122 sets AF push-pull with no pull, so a temporary OD-with-pull-up reconfig and restore is a small, contained change), there is no MISO readback (secure/src/board/pq1.rs:103 `LCD_MISO_PIN = None`), and docs/security/user-device-verification.md:163-168 indeed lists the LCD-SPI logger as an undefended residual. Flash cost is a few KB, and the no-battery constraint is irrelevant (no latched state is needed). The proposal is therefore not refuted, but as written it has two design errors that would make it miss the realistic implant or let the targeted attacker trivially re-enrol, and it collides with an existing first-boot check; these are corrections, not a bypass of the concept. I could not verify the vendor-precedent claims (Grand slides content, the 2026-10-09 CoinDesk story is after my knowledge) and did not parse the PCB PDFs (docs/hardware/schematics/ is empty), so external pull-ups/series resistors on the CS/SCK lines are unknown.
feasible.corrections:
1. RATIOMETRIC-ONLY DETECTION FAILS ON THE REAL IMPLANT. An SPI sniffer taps SCK, MOSI, CS (and DC) together with similar input pins, adding roughly the same few pF to every line; the line-vs-line ratios the proposal relies on barely move. The check must be ABSOLUTE with a common-mode reference the implant has no reason to touch: on pq1 use the NC pad PA6 (pin bonded, unrouted; today the TIM3_CH1 consumption-mask pin, so the mask must be paused and the pin reconfigured) as tau_ref = R_pu * C_pad to cancel pull-up corner, VDD and temperature, then compare each line's C = C_pad * t_line/t_ref against a per-device absolute band. Pin-to-pin pull-up mismatch on the same die remains uncancelled and must be characterised. Also measure both rise (pull-up) and fall (pull-down) to cancel Schmitt-threshold drift; the ADC temperature sensor is optional and would need ADC1 added to the GTZC secure allocation (secure/src/sau.rs does not secure any ADC today).
2. A FACTORY-WRITTEN FLASH PAGE IS WORTHLESS AGAINST THE STATED ATTACKER. The shipping model (CLAUDE.md invariant #10, first_boot/mod.rs) ships at RDP-0 with SWD open until first field boot; a reseller inserting an implant can simply rewrite the baseline page over SWD after re-measuring. The baseline must be in OTP (176 of 512 B are used per secure/src/hw/otp.rs:131-190, so there is room) in a fixed single-use quad-word slot with a bit-clear-resistant encoding (a hash/CRC over the band, since OTP bits can still be driven 1->0 after programming), or be a factory-C10-signed record verified against a pinned factory verification key. Note that even so the enrolment trust is exactly the open, not-yet-approved per-unit factory handoff (S-1/S-2-class ceremony), and the record is per-device data the user cannot reproduce from the build - only its format/signature is verifiable over SWD.
3. PAGE COLLISION. first_boot/mod.rs:197-205 (R2.2) halts the first field boot if ANY of pages 123..=127 is non-blank; "a per-device page" in that range is therefore a hard conflict with the rdp2-self-lock candidate. Either amend R2.2 with a dedicated page outside 123..127 (and re-review the blank-check argument) or use OTP.
4. ENROLMENT NEEDS THE DEVICE POWERED WITH THE FINAL PANEL+FLEX INSTALLED IN THE FINAL ENCLOSURE, under a factory/prodtest image (make build-hw-prodtest), not the production image (which would self-lock on first power); the capacitance depends on the assembled mechanical stack. The measurement state must match enrolment: the panel must be powered (VDD1/LCM rails up), since driving a line high into an unpowered NV3007 forward-biases its ESD clamps and corrupts the decay; CS must be high during SCK/MOSI tests, and testing CS itself gives the panel a clock-less CS pulse (harmless but should be confirmed on silicon).
5. SCOPE GAP: the PIN and the RESTORE-WIZARD words are also fully recoverable from the BUTTON lines (PA0 LEFT, etc.) - a logger on the two keys recovers the PIN digit-selection sequence without touching the display. The display check protects the seed-display wizard; the same decay test should be extended to the button nets (harder: switch + any external pull-up), or the residual stated.
6. RESOLUTION: a polling loop samples IDR every ~5-8 cycles, i.e. 3-8% quantisation on a ~100-190-cycle decay, and repetition does not average away quantisation without jitter; prefer TIM input capture where a channel exists (PA5 is TIM2_CH1, already secured; PA7 is TIM3_CH2; PA4 has no timer channel) or accept a coarser band. Pull-up tolerance (25-55k) is a factory-enrolment per-device matter, not a per-boot one, once the reference pin cancels it.
7. COST/PRIORITY: the firmware is M, but the >=5-unit thermal/humidity/ageing validation plus the factory-ceremony and OTP-format work makes it M-to-L overall; given the stated ~1 pF floor, the button-line gap and its dependency on the unclosed factory handoff, P2 behind closing S-1/S-2 is more honest than P1. The threat-model premise that "the one real implant sat on the display bus" and the CoinDesk/Grand citations are unverified by me.

vendor-claim.reason: Precedent and novelty claims hold. (1) Trezor ships nothing of this kind: the only tamper machinery in /home/nicola/repos/trezor-firmware (HEAD 6ab39e95, 2026-10-07) is the STM32U5 TAMP peripheral — internal tampers ITAMP1/2/3/5/6/7/8/9/11/12/13 (core/embed/sec/tamper/stm32u5/tamper.c:140-152) plus one passive external tamper input on T3W1 (`#define TAMPER_INPUT_2 1`, core/embed/models/T3W1/boards/trezor_t3w1_revC.h:326; read by prodtest `tamper-read`, core/embed/projects/prodtest/cmd/prodtest_tamper.c:29-53). A grep for capacit|rise.?time|decay|impedance|implant|interposer over core/embed and docs returns only battery-capacity, NFC antenna-tuning and SD-card hits; no display-bus electrical self-check exists. Display drivers (core/embed/io/display/*) have no panel-ID readback or bus fingerprint. (2) Ledger: Grand's hardwear.io 2026 slides (downloaded, 134,738,515 B, pdftotext) confirm the Nano X implant "monitors SPI traffic between Nano X Secure Element and OLED", uses "template matcher functions" on a-z glyphs, stores the seed at flash 0x7000 and transmits "over 4G LTE" via an Air700 cellular module with eSIM (slides2.txt:81-99, 195-205, 232-236); the "LEDGER RESPONSE" slide is exactly "Check hardware integrity against known-good pictures / Follow best practices when buying a device – Directly from Ledger or authorized resellers / Ledger is looking into further hardening for future products" (slides2.txt:221-228). Ledger's 2026-10-10 statement confirms "an unauthorized hardware implant" in an affected CryptoBilis-sold device and only says it is "working on further, enhanced anti-tampering solutions" — nothing shipped (news.bitcoin.com). The Coindesk 2026-10-09 source exists and matches the proposal's reseller-stage framing (no detection measures mentioned). (3) PACTOR: IEEE Spectrum (2024-02-28) confirms Columbia (Seok/Li) with Intel's Vivek De, ISSCC, capacitance change "as small as 0.5 pF" on processor-memory PCB traces, and that v1 false-alarmed hot / missed cold so a temperature sensor now selects the threshold — the proposal's "temperature-selected threshold their v2 needed" is supported. Columbia news page returned HTTP 403 on fetch; search-engine summary corroborates it repeats the Spectrum account. (4) No vendor (Ledger, Trezor, Coldcard, BitBox, Keystone, GridPlus) ships a bus-capacitance/impedance self-check; GridPlus Lattice1 ships an enclosure anti-tamper mesh (docs.gridplus.io/lattice1/security-features), Coldcard a clear case + bag number, Ledger Stax/Flex an SE-driven E-Ink screen — all different mechanisms. Academic precedent beyond PACTOR exists (PDNPulse TIFS 2023, CaLIAD/LAPD/ROPAD+, TI/other RC-time-constant tamper patents), so 'beyond' is correct for vendor novelty but the idea is not academically novel. (5) Repo evidence verified at the cited lines: pq1.rs:96-103 (`LCD_MISO_PIN = None`), lcd_nv3007.rs:277-291 (#705 analog-mode IDR lesson), spi_hw.rs:116-122 (AF push-pull, no pull), user-device-verification.md:163-168, threat-model.md:343.
vendor-claim.corrections: (a) vendor_precedent says PACTOR senses "sub-0.5 pF"; Spectrum says "as small as 0.5 picofarads" — write "≈0.5 pF", not sub-0.5. (b) The sentence "Ledger's recorded implant response is photos + authorised resellers only" should add the third bullet from the slide, "Ledger is looking into further hardening for future products", and Ledger's 2026-10-10 statement that it is "working on further, enhanced anti-tampering solutions" (nothing shipped as of 2026-10-11). (c) Important framing correction: on the Nano X the OLED is driven DIRECTLY by the Secure Element (slides2.txt:89 "OLED connects to the Nano X Secure Element via SPI") and the implant still captured the seed — so Ledger's shipped "secure screen = SE drives the display" architecture (Stax/Flex) is NOT a mitigation for this threat class; cite this to pre-empt "Ledger already solved it" pushback. (d) repo_evidence grep claim "IDR/capacit/rise-time … none" is literally wrong: `IDR` hits at lcd_nv3007.rs:277-291 (the retracted #705 probe comment the proposal already cites) and "capacitive load" at spi_hw.rs:227 (a comment explaining the iota2 LD2-on-PE13 SCK edge rounding, no measurement code). Substance unchanged: no measurement path exists. Incidentally spi_hw.rs:222-232 is useful supporting evidence that SCK on this bus is already sensitive to a few-pF parasitic (LED+resistor on SCK caused misread bits at 40 MHz). (e) Repo conflict to state in risks: the factory-enrolled baseline page collides with the rdp2-self-lock first-boot gate, which halts with `PerDevicePageNotBlank` unless pages 123..=127 are all blank (secure/src/first_boot/mod.rs:197-203, `flash::is_secure_page_blank`) — enrolment must use OTP, a page outside 123-127, or an approved change to that blank-check. (f) There is no ADC / internal-temperature-sensor driver in secure/src/hw/ (listing: no adc.rs; grep ADC|TSEN|VSENSE over secure/src/hw finds nothing), so the proposed temperature compensation adds a new secured-peripheral driver plus a GTZC/SAU allowlist entry (invariant #4 adjacent) — raise cost from M or note it explicitly. (g) Closest Trezor precedent to cite instead of "none": passive TAMP external tamper input on T3W1 (trezor_t3w1_revC.h:326, tamper.c external_read) and the same internal ITAMP set that PQSigner already ports (secure/src/hw/tamp.rs:30-41); and STM32U5 'active tamper' (ATAMP output→input loop, Microchip calls the equivalent "active layer protection") is a silicon-shipped digital loop-back trace monitor — a related but weaker (continuity, not capacitance) mechanism. (h) Mask pin note: on pq1 the mask is PA6/TIM3_CH1 (consumption_mask.rs:31) and SCK is PA5 — adjacent, as stated; on iota2 the mask itself is PA5 but the LCD SPI lives on PE12..15 there, so no conflict on either board; still pause the mask during the test as proposed.
